finding: In normal gravity (1g), an 8-fold density gradient across 1 cm (2,300 K flame vs 300 K ambient) induces buoyant velocity fields that dominate and obscure chemistry. In microgravity, buoyancy is suppressed, reducing flame dynamics to 1D quiescent diffusion.
topics: fundamental physics; buoyancy; density gradient; flame temperature; 1d diffusion
source_title: NASA Glenn Research Center: Combustion Science Discipline Overview
note: NASA Glenn physical sciences discipline framework explaining why microgravity simplifies 3D turbulent buoyancy to 1D computable diffusion.

finding: The Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2) investigation demonstrates that materials (such as cotton-fiberglass SIBAL fabric) can burn at lower oxygen concentrations in lunar gravity (1/6g) than in 1g Earth gravity, indicating standard Earth flammability tests (NASA-STD-6001) may underestimate fire risk on lunar surfaces.
topics: lunar combustion; FM2; sibal fabric; partial gravity; flammability boundary; NASA-STD-6001
source_title: NASA Glenn Research Center: Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2)
note: Corroborated by drop tower centrifuge and ISS microgravity tests of SIBAL fabric burning in simulated lunar gravity.
